result.summary: Removes legacy reverse-precedence handling in SettingsValue GetSetting, making later settings take precedence over earlier ones across all sources. This backward-compatibility quirk is rendered obsolete once prerequisite PR #17493 forbids multiple assignments to single-value settings in configuration files.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's settings parser historically used reverse precedence for configuration files, where the first assigned value took priority over later values instead of standard last-wins precedence. This added complexity and special-casing to settings interpretation.
evidence: PR description: 'This change implements one of the settings simplifications listed in #17508.'
PR description: 'This has no effect on behavior because as of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/17493 it's not possible to specify multiple values for single value settings in the config file.'
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on #16545, #17580, and #17493. Only the final commit (`4bff8012d0`) is unique to this PR, touching only src/common/settings.cpp and src/test/settings_tests.cpp.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased on updated base PRs; the core change remains identical.
result.card: This PR removes the legacy reverse-precedence logic in settings parsing, aligning config file setting resolution with the standard last-setting-wins rule. Because dependent PR #17493 forbids duplicate assignments to single-value settings in configuration files, this code path is redundant and the change introduces no behavioral changes. It is part of the settings simplifications tracked in issue #17508 and depends on PRs #16545, #17493, and #17580.

risk.why: A flaw in setting resolution logic could result in incorrect configuration values being selected on startup.
